children.name: Cephalopyrus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Fire-capped Tit, a small greenish-yellow tit of the Himalayan foothills with a brilliant orange-red crown patch. It was once placed in the penduline tit family Remizidae but molecular studies place it firmly within Paridae.

children.name: Cephalopyrus flammiceps
children.description: The fire-capped tit (Cephalopyrus flammiceps) is a small, long, weighing about bird species assigned to the family Paridae, that breeds in the temperate forest bordering the Himalayas to the south, in the Hengduan Shan and Nujiang Shan on the Myanmar-China border, the Micah Shan and Daba Shan on the Northern Sichuan border. It winters down hill and further south. Further to the east, birds tend to be smaller and the plumage becomes gradually darker.

children.name: Parus
children.description: The great tits — large, bold members of the family with striking black-and-yellow plumage and a versatile, opportunistic diet. The Great Tit is one of the most studied birds in the world, a model organism for research into ecology, behaviour, and the evolutionary consequences of urbanisation. Its two-note song is famously variable and can be rendered in dozens of dialects across its range.

children.name: Parus major
children.description: The great tit is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is widespread and common throughout Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia and as far east as the Amur River. It also occurs in parts of North Africa where it is generally resident in any sort of woodland.

children.name: Parus minor
children.description: The cinereous tit or Asian tit (Parus cinereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Parus monticolus
children.description:
The green-backed tit (Parus monticolus) is a species of bird in the family Paridae.
It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Taiwan and Vietnam.

children.name: Parus cinereus
children.description: The cinereous tit or Asian tit (Parus cinereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Parus bokharensis
children.description: The great tit (Parus major) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Parus ater
children.description: Parus ater (Coal Tit) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Parus caeruleus
children.description: Parus caeruleus (Blue Tit) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.description: Parus cristatus (Crested Tit) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.description: Parus lugubris (Sombre Tit) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Parus montanus
children.description: Parus montanus (Willow Tit) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Parus palustris

children.name: Parus cinctus
children.description: Parus cinctus (Siberian Tit) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Parus cyanus

children.name: Parus teneriffae
children.description: Parus teneriffae is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Parus atricapillus
children.description: Parus atricapillus (Black-Capped Chickadee) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Parus hudsonicus
children.description: Parus hudsonicus (Boreal Chickadee) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Parus rhenanus

children.name: Parus corsus

children.name: Parus sardus

children.name: Parus dresseri
children.description: Parus dresseri is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Parus songarus

children.name: Parus aplonotus
children.description: Parus aplonotus (Indian Black-lored Tit) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Cyanistes
children.description: The blue tits — small, acrobatic tits with vivid blue-and-yellow plumage. The Eurasian Blue Tit (Blåmes) is one of the most familiar garden birds across Europe, famous for its ability to hang upside-down on the outermost branches to reach insects, and for its habit of opening milk bottle tops — a learned behaviour that spread across Britain in the 20th century.

children.name: Cyanistes caeruleus
children.description: The Eurasian blue tit is a small passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is easily recognised by its blue and yellow plumage and small size.

children.name: Cyanistes cyanus
children.description: The azure tit is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder throughout Russia, Central Asia, northwest China, Manchuria, and Pakistan.

children.name: Cyanistes teneriffae
children.description: The African blue tit (Cyanistes teneriffae) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. It is found in northern Africa, Pantelleria (Italy) and the Canary Islands (Spain). Its natural habitat is temperate forests. This species and the Eurasian blue tit were formerly considered conspecific. The status of this species has not been assessed because it is noted to be common on the islands of Tenerife and Gran Canaria. The species has been used in many research studies due to its island populations and relevance to evolutionary hypotheses.

children.name: Cyanistes ×caeruleus
children.description: Cyanistes ×caeruleus is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Cyanistes ×cyanus
children.description: Cyanistes ×cyanus is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Cyanistes ultramarinus
children.description: Cyanistes ultramarinus is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Cyanistes flavipectus
children.description: Cyanistes flavipectus is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Cyanistes palmensis
children.description: Cyanistes palmensis is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Cyanistes degener
children.description: Cyanistes degener is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Cyanistes ombriosus
children.description: Cyanistes ombriosus is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Periparus
children.description: Small, dark tits of coniferous forests, distinguished by their glossy black cap and bib. The Coal Tit is the most widespread, a diminutive bird that hoards food in winter — tiny caches of seeds and insects secreted in bark crevices, which it can remember and retrieve weeks later.

children.name: Periparus ater
children.description: The coal tit is a passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder in forests throughout the temperate to subtropical Palearctic, including North Africa. The black-crested tit is now included in this species.

children.name: Periparus rubidiventris
children.description: The rufous-vented tit (Periparus rubidiventris) is an Asian songbird species in the tit and chickadee family (Paridae). Some of its subspecies were formerly assigned to its western relative the rufous-naped tit (P. Rufonuchalis), or these two were considered entirely conspecific.

children.name: Periparus melanolophus
children.description: The black-crested tit (Periparus ater melanolophus), also known as the spot-winged tit, is a bird in the family Paridae. It was formerly considered a distinct species, but is now considered a subspecies of the coal tit.

children.name: Periparus rufonuchalis
children.description:
The rufous-naped tit (Periparus rufonuchalis), also known as the black-breasted tit or dark-grey tit, is an Asian songbird species in the tit and chickadee family (Paridae). It was sometimes considered conspecific with the rufous-vented tit (P. Rubidiventris), and was formerly placed in the genus Parus.
This tit is a native of the western Himalayas, but has a very large range, occurring in parts of India, China, Pakistan, Turkestan, Kyrgyzstan, and Afghanistan. Widespread and common, it is not considered a threatened species by the IUCN.

children.name: Periparus venustulus
children.description: Periparus venustulus (Yellow-bellied Tit) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Periparus elegans
children.description: Periparus elegans (Elegant Tit) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Periparus amabilis
children.description: Periparus amabilis (Palawan Tit) is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Periparus ×ater
children.description: Periparus ×ater is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Pardaliparus
children.description: Small, brightly coloured tits of East and Southeast Asian forests, formerly included in Periparus. The Yellow-bellied Tit is one of the most beautiful members of the family, resembling a living jewel with its black-and-yellow plumage and white crescent on the nape.

children.name: Pardaliparus venustulus
children.description: Pardaliparus venustulus (Yellow-bellied Tit) is a miscellaneous tits species found in Asia region.

children.name: Pardaliparus elegans
children.description: The elegant tit (Periparus elegans) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Pardaliparus amabilis
children.description: The Palawan tit (Periparus amabilis) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile
children.description: Marsh and willow tits of the northern Palearctic — drab but charming birds in brown and white, best told apart by their calls. The Willow Tit excavates its own nest hole in rotten wood, while the Marsh Tit takes over existing cavities. The Siberian Tit is one of the hardiest passerines on Earth, surviving Arctic winters through shivering, food caching, and a remarkably high metabolic rate. In North America the genus includes the chickadees, among the most familiar and beloved backyard birds on the continent.

children.name: Poecile palustris
children.description: The marsh tit is a Eurasian passerine bird in the tit family Paridae and genus Poecile, closely related to the willow tit, Père David's and Songar tits. It is a small bird, around 12 cm (4.7 in) long and weighing 12 g (0.42 oz), with a black crown and nape, pale cheeks, brown back and greyish-brown wings and tail. Between 8 and 11 subspecies are recognised.

children.name: Poecile montanus
children.description: The willow tit is a passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder throughout temperate and subarctic Europe and across the Palearctic. The plumage is grey-brown and off-white with a black cap and bib.

children.name: Poecile lugubris
children.description: The sombre tit (Poecile lugubris) is a species of passerine bird belonging to the family Paridae, the "true" tits and chickadees.

children.name: Poecile cinctus
children.description: The grey-headed chickadee or Siberian tit is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is a widespread resident breeder throughout subarctic Scandinavia and the northern Palearctic, and also into North America in Alaska and the far northwest of Canada. It is a conifer specialist.

children.name: Poecile davidi
children.description:
Père David's tit or the rusty-breasted tit (Poecile davidi) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae. It is endemic to central China in southern Gansu, western Hubei, southern Shaanxi and Sichuan.
It is long with a weight, and is similar to the related sombre tit (P. Lugubris) in appearance, with a black head with white cheeks, dark grey-brown back, wings and tail, and rusty brown underparts.

children.name: Poecile atricapillus
children.description:
The black-capped chickadee (Poecile atricapillus) is a small, nonmigratory, North American passerine bird that lives in deciduous and mixed forests. It is a member of the Paridae family, also known as tits. It has a distinct black cap on its head, a black bib underneath, and white cheeks. It has a white belly, buff sides, and grey wings, back, and tail. The bird is well known for its vocalizations, including its fee-bee song and its chick-a-dee-dee-dee call, from which it derives its name.
The black-capped chickadee is widely distributed throughout North America, ranging from the northern United States to southern Canada and all the way up to Alaska and Yukon. It feeds primarily on insects and seeds, and is known for its ability to cache food for use during the winter. The hippocampus of the black-capped chickadee grows during the caching season, which is believed to help it better remember its cache locations. The black-capped chickadee is a social bird and forms strict dominance hierarchies within its flock. During the winter, these flocks include other bird species. It has the ability to lower its body temperature during cold winter nights, allowing it to conserve energy.

children.name: Poecile carolinensis
children.description: The Carolina chickadee (Poecile carolinensis) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile gambeli
children.description: The mountain chickadee (Poecile gambeli) is a small songbird, a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile rufescens
children.description: The chestnut-backed chickadee (Poecile rufescens) is a small passerine bird in the tit family, native to western North America.

children.name: Poecile hudsonicus
children.description: The boreal chickadee (Poecile hudsonicus) is a small passerine songbird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile sclateri
children.description: The Mexican chickadee (Poecile sclateri) is a small passerine songbird in the family Paridae, the tits and chickadees.

children.name: Poecile hypermelaenus
children.description: The black-bibbed tit (Poecile hypermelaenus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae. It is found from central and eastern China to southeast Tibet and western Myanmar.

children.name: Poecile weigoldicus
children.description: The Sichuan tit (Poecile weigoldicus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Poecile superciliosus
children.description:
The white-browed tit (Poecile superciliosus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae. It is endemic to the mountain forests of central China and Tibet.
It is 13.5–14 cm long, with a weight of 10–12 g. The plumage pattern is very similar to that of the western North American mountain chickadee P. Gambeli (of which it has on occasion been considered a subspecies, despite its being on a different continent), differing in the breast and cheeks being rusty brown, not white, and having a longer and more sharply defined white eyebrow; the back is also a richer brown, not greyish-brown (del Hoyo et al. 2007).

children.name: Poecile songarus
children.description: The Songar tit (Poecile montanus songarus) is a passerine bird in the tit family.

children.name: Poecile hyrcanus
children.description: Poecile hyrcanus (Caspian Tit) is a marsh tits species found in its native region.

children.name: Poecile ×montanus
children.description: Poecile ×montanus is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Poecile ×palustris
children.description: Poecile ×palustris is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Poecile ×cinctus
children.description: Poecile ×cinctus is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Poecile sp.
children.description: Poecile sp. is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Sittiparus
children.description: Varied tits of East Asia, recently split from Poecile based on genetic and morphological differences. These are colourful, pattern-faced tits restricted to islands and coastal regions of Japan, Taiwan, and eastern China.

children.name: Sittiparus varius
children.description: The varied tit (Sittiparus varius) is a perching bird from the tit family, Paridae.

children.name: Sittiparus ierardi
children.description: Endemic to the Izu Islands south of Tokyo, this tit differs from the Varied Tit in its darker belly and reduced white on the face. It is a restricted-range species vulnerable to introduced predators.

children.name: Sittiparus owstoni
children.description:
Owston's tit (Sittiparus owstoni) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae that is endemic to the southern Izu Islands south of Japan, occurring only on the islands of Miyakejima, Mikurajima and Hachijojima.
Owston's tit was formerly considered as subspecies of the varied tit but was promoted to species status based on the results of a phylogenetic study published in 2014. The species was first described by Ijima Isao in 1893, based on two females from Miyake-jima obtained by Alan Owston's collector, and named Parus owstoni in his honour. This was the first description of a bird by a zoologist from Japan.

children.name: Sittiparus castaneoventris
children.description:
The chestnut-bellied tit (Sittiparus castaneoventris) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae that is endemic to Taiwan.
The chestnut-bellied tit was first described by the English ornithologist John Gould in 1863 and given the binomial name Parus castaneoventris. It was formerly considered as a subspecies of the varied tit but was promoted to species status after the publication of a phylogenetic study in 2014.

children.name: Sittiparus olivaceus
children.description: Sittiparus olivaceus (Iriomote Tit) is a marsh tits species found in its native region.

children.name: Sittiparus semilarvatus
children.description: Sittiparus semilarvatus (White-fronted Tit) is a marsh tits species found in its native region.

children.name: Sylviparus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Yellow-browed Tit, a tiny, olive-green leaf-gleaning tit of Asian forests with a distinct warbler-like appearance and habits.

children.name: Sylviparus modestus
children.description:
The yellow-browed tit (Sylviparus modestus) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. It is placed in the monotypic genus Sylviparus. It is a small song bird that measures 9–10 cm long (~3.6.) and weighs 5–9 g. It is the smallest member of its family. It has a small bill, short tail, strong legs, and greenish feathers.
It is found in the southern Himalayas, Northeast India and southern China with smaller amounts in Southeast Asia. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Lophophanes
children.description: Crested tits — recognisable at a glance by their spiky, black-and-white crest, unique among European tits. The Crested Tit is a specialist of mature pine forests and rarely strays far from them, making it one of the few European birds that cannot easily recolonise areas after deforestation. It too caches food extensively through winter.

children.name: Lophophanes cristatus
children.description: The crested tit or European crested tit is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder in coniferous forests throughout central and northern Europe and in deciduous woodland in France and the Iberian Peninsula. In Great Britain, it is mainly restricted to the ancient pinewoods of Inverness and Strathspey in Scotland, and rarely strays far from its haunts.

children.name: Lophophanes dichrous
children.description:
The grey-crested tit (Lophophanes dichrous) is a species of bird in the family Paridae.
It is found in the Himalayan foothills and southern-central China. Its natural habitats are temperate forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Machlolophus
children.description: Yellow-crested tits of South and East Asia, with striking sulphur-yellow crests and underparts. They inhabit broadleaf and mixed forests from the foothills of the Himalayas to the islands of Japan and Taiwan, filling a similar ecological niche to the great tits of the western Palearctic.

children.name: Machlolophus spilonotus
children.description:
The yellow-cheeked tit (Machlolophus spilonotus) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest. It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, Hong Kong, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam.
The yellow-cheeked tit was formerly one of the many species in the genus Parus but was moved to Machlolophus after a molecular phylogenetic analysis published in 2013 showed that the members of the new genus formed a distinct clade.

children.name: Machlolophus holsti
children.description: The yellow tit (Machlolophus holsti), also known as Taiwan yellow tit and Formosan yellow tit is a species of bird in the family Paridae.

children.name: Machlolophus xanthogenys
children.description: The Himalayan black-lored tit (Machlolophus xanthogenys), also known as simply black-lored tit, is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Machlolophus aplonotus
children.description:
The Indian black-lored tit, Indian tit, or Indian yellow tit (Grimmett et al., 2011) (Machlolophus aplonotus) is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. The yellow-cheeked tit is probably its closest relative, and both may be related to the yellow tit. These three tits almost certainly form a distinct lineage as evidenced by morphology, and mtDNA cytochrome b sequence analysis (Gill et al., 2005). The subgenus name Macholophus may apply for them.
This species is a resident breeder on the Indian subcontinent. It is a common bird in open tropical forests, but does not occur in Sri Lanka. It is an active and agile feeder, taking insects and spiders from the canopy, and sometimes fruit.

children.name: Machlolophus nuchalis
children.description:
The white-naped tit (Machlolophus nuchalis), sometimes called white-winged tit, is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is endemic to India where it is found in dry thorn scrub forest in two disjunct populations, in western India and southern India. Its specific name nuchalis means 'of the nuchal, nape'.
This species is hard to mistake with its contrasting black and white patterns without the grey wing coverts and back of the partly sympatric cinereous tit (Parus cinereus). This species is very patchily distributed and has been considered to be vulnerable to extinction especially because of the scarcity of suitable habitats particularly nest cavities made by woodpeckers.

children.name: Melaniparus
children.description: African black tits — the continent's dominant tit group, replacing the Eurasian Parus in sub-Saharan Africa. Most species are predominantly black with white or yellow markings, and many show striking white wing patches. They are active, acrobatic foragers in acacia savanna, miombo woodland, and montane forest across the whole of sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Melaniparus niger
children.description: The southern black tit or simply black tit (Melaniparus niger) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae, which is native to woodland habitats in southern Africa.

children.name: Melaniparus carpi
children.description:
Carp's tit (Melaniparus carpi) or Carp's black tit, is a species of bird in the family Paridae. Some authors consider it a subspecies of the black tit. It is found throughout the Namibian savanna woodlands and the southern Angolan mopane woodlands.
Its name commemorates olympic sailor and ornithologist Berend Carp (1901-1966).

children.name: Melaniparus albiventris
children.description:
The white-bellied tit (Melaniparus albiventris) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. It is found in Cameroon, Kenya, Nigeria, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
The white-bellied tit was formerly one of the many species in the genus Parus but was moved to Melaniparus after a molecular phylogenetic analysis published in 2013 showed that the members of the new genus formed a distinct clade.

children.name: Melaniparus leuconotus
children.description:
The white-backed black tit (Melaniparus leuconotus), also known as the white-backed tit, is a species of bird in the family Paridae. It is found in Eritrea and Ethiopia. Its natural habitat is boreal forests.
The white-backed black tit was formerly one of the many species in the genus Parus but was moved to Melaniparus after a molecular phylogenetic analysis published in 2013 showed that the members of the new genus formed a distinct clade.

children.name: Melaniparus funereus
children.description: Melaniparus funereus (Dusky Tit) is a african tits species found in Africa region.

children.name: Melaniparus rufiventris
children.description: The rufous-bellied tit (Melaniparus rufiventris) is a species of bird in the tit family. It is found in Africa from the Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo and northern Namibia east to Tanzania and northern Mozambique.

children.name: Melaniparus pallidiventris
children.description: The rufous-bellied tit (Melaniparus rufiventris) is a species of bird in the tit family. It is found in Africa from the Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo and northern Namibia east to Tanzania and northern Mozambique.

children.name: Melaniparus fringillinus
children.description:
The red-throated tit (Melaniparus fringillinus) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. It is found in Kenya and Tanzania, where its natural habitat is dry savanna.
The red-throated tit was formerly one of the many species in the genus Parus but was moved to Melaniparus after a molecular phylogenetic analysis published in 2013 showed that the members of the new genus formed a distinct clade.

children.name: Melaniparus fasciiventer
children.description:
The stripe-breasted tit (Melaniparus fasciiventer) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. It is native to the Albertine Rift montane forests in east-central Africa.
The stripe-breasted tit was formerly one of the many species in the genus Parus but was moved to Melaniparus after a molecular phylogenetic analysis published in 2013 showed that the members of the new genus formed a distinct clade.

children.name: Melaniparus semilarvatus
children.description: A large, glossy black tit with a large white shoulder patch, endemic to the lowland forests of West Africa. It is a specialised forest interior species, scarce and local throughout its range.

children.name: Melaniparus griseiventris
children.description: The miombo tit (Melaniparus griseiventris) is a species of bird in the family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus cinerascens
children.description: The ashy tit (Melaniparus cinerascens) is a species of bird in the family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus afer
children.description: The grey tit (Melaniparus afer) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Melaniparus leucomelas
children.description: The white-winged black tit (Melaniparus leucomelas) is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is also known as the white-winged tit, dark-eyed black tit or northern black tit. The species was first described by Eduard Rüppell in 1840.

children.name: Melaniparus guineensis
children.description:
The white-shouldered black tit (Melaniparus guineensis), also known as the pale-eyed black tit, is a passerine bird in the tit family. It breeds in a belt across Africa from Senegal in the west to Kenya and Ethiopia in the east. It is sometimes considered conspecific with the more southerly white-winged black tit Melaniparus leucomelas and, like that species, it is mainly black with a white wing patch, but differs in that it has a pale eye.
It is a resident in coniferous woodlands throughout its range, and nests in tree crevice. 4-6 reddish-brown blotched pinkish-white eggs are laid.

children.name: Melaniparus thruppi
children.description: Melaniparus thruppi (Acacia Tit) is a african tits species found in its native region.

children.name: Pseudopodoces
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Ground Tit of the Tibetan Plateau — a remarkable bird long classified as a crow relative due to its terrestrial habits and decurved bill. Molecular analysis revealed it to be a highly modified parid that has adapted to life above the treeline, nesting in rodent burrows and feeding on invertebrates in the sparse alpine steppe.

children.name: Pseudopodoces humilis
children.description: The ground tit, Tibetan ground tit, or Hume's ground tit (Pseudopodoces humilis) is a bird of the Tibetan plateau north of the Himalayas.

children.name: Baeolophus
children.description: The titmice of North America — small grey crested tits that are bold, vocal visitors to woodlands and feeders across the United States and Mexico.

children.name: Baeolophus bicolor
children.description: The tufted titmouse (Baeolophus bicolor) is a small songbird native to eastern North America.

children.name: Baeolophus atricristatus
children.description: The black-crested titmouse or Mexican titmouse (Baeolophus atricristatus), is a passerine bird in the family Paridae, the tits and chickadees. It is found in Mexico and the U. S. States of Oklahoma and Texas and as a vagrant in at least one other state.

children.name: Baeolophus inornatus
children.description: Baeolophus inornatus (Oak Titmouse) is a titmice species found in North America region.

children.name: Baeolophus wollweberi
children.description: The bridled titmouse (Baeolophus wollweberi) is a small passerine bird in the family Paridae, the tits and chickadees.

children.name: Baeolophus ridgwayi
children.description: The juniper titmouse (Baeolophus ridgwayi) is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

children.name: Baeolophus ×atricristatus
children.description: Baeolophus ×atricristatus is a paridae species found in its native region.

children.name: Melanochlora
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Sultan Tit, by far the largest member of the family, a crested black-and-yellow giant of Southeast Asian forests.

children.name: Melanochlora sultanea
children.description: The sultan tit (Melanochlora sultanea) is an Asian forest bird with black upperparts plumage and yellow underparts, dark bill, and (depending on subspecies) a yellow or black crest.
